Resemble

/rih-ZEM-buhl/ · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Resemble means to look or seem similar to someone or something else.

With her sharp wit and stubborn chin, the girl resembled her grandmother far more than either of her parents.

Worked Example

Paleontologists studying the newly unearthed fossil noted that its long neck and small head made it resemble a modern giraffe far more closely than any dinosaur previously found in the region, despite the sixty-million-year gap between them.

The fossil isn't a giraffe and isn't related to one, but its shape looks similar enough to invite the comparison — which is exactly what "resemble" describes: an outward similarity, whether or not it reflects a true connection.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

look like: the simplest, most everyday phrase for the same idea

take after: specifically used for family resemblance

mirror: suggests an especially close, almost exact similarity

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

differ from: the direct opposite — being unlike something

contrast with: emphasizes a striking, noticeable difference

Where it sits · how closely the two match — look like → resemble → mirror

look like vs. resemble: Look like is weaker than resemble: two strangers might look like each other in a passing, surface way, while resembling someone suggests a deeper, more thorough likeness.

mirror vs. resemble: Mirror is stronger than resemble: things that merely resemble each other share some features, while mirroring goes further, matching so exactly that one seems a reflection of the other.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-

Prefix — re-: again, intensively

Root — sembl-

Root — sembl-: like, similar (Latin similis, via Old French sembler)

Put it together

Put it together: "Resemble" builds on the same sembl- root found in "similar" and "assemble" — the re- prefix here intensifies the idea, so that resembling something means seeming genuinely like it.

Use the root in a new word: semblance

Use the root in a new word: semblance: After the storm, the crew worked through the night just to restore some semblance of order to the flooded warehouse.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral, everyday

Resemble is a common, neutral verb for describing similarity — physical, behavioral, or structural. It makes no claim about whether the similarity is coincidental, inherited, or intentional.
